newsitem.title: CHINA: China Jan-Sept industry output up 12.9 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: China Jan-Sept industry output up 12.9 pct yr/yr.

text.p: China's industrial output rose by 12.9 percent to 1,357.5 billion yuan in the first nine months of this year compared with the year-ago period, the State Statistical Bureau said on Wednesday.
It did not give a figure for September output. August industrial output rose by a year-on-year 10.6 percent, the lowest monthly growth seen this year.
Output of companies wholly owned or majority controlled by the state was up by 5.7 percent compared with the year-ago period, of that output state-owned enterprises alone was up by 5.5 percent.
Output of collective enterprises soared by 17.9 percent year-on-year and that of private enterprises rose by 13.4 percent.

The bureau said the growth rate had slowed in the first nine months, with industrial output growing by 13.6 percent in the first quarter, 13.1 percent in the second quarter and 11.8 percent in the third quarter.
The output of non-state enterprises had grown rather more quickly while output of state-owned enterprises was comparatively slow, the bureau said.
Output of light industry grew by 13.3 percent to 553.3 billion yuan in January-September while output of heavy industry rose by 12.5 percent to 804.2 billion yuan.
Production of primary energy products reached 930 million tonnes, up by 7.6 percent with coal output up by 8.0 percent and crude oil up by 6.2 percent.

The bureau cited the most striking problems facing China's industry as a poor link between sales and production -- a hint that stockpiles remained high -- as well as a continuing rise in triangular debt, or debt among enterprises, and declining efficiency.
